title: Ofgem announces the energy price cap for 1 January to 31 March 2027 — the step that sets the January UK CPI energy contribution and the first cap the MPC forecasts after the November MPR
source: EST: ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-october-and-31-december-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — Ofgem's own 26 August 2026 cap release states that the following quarter's rates, covering 1 January to 31 March 2027, will be announced by 25 November 2026. The same release sets the 1 October to 31 December 2026 cap at a 4% rise for a typical direct-debit household (electricity 26.32p/kWh with a 54.83p/day standing charge; gas 7.97p/kWh with a 29.68p/day standing charge) and records that 'The government has removed VAT from electricity bills from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027', so 'VAT is not included in electricity bills for people covered under the energy price cap between 1 October and 31 December 2026' while gas stays at 5%. Filed estimate on two counts: Ofgem words the date as an 'by' commitment rather than a fixed publication slot, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a UK sector regulator. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2026-10-21, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-cpi-2026-10-21 LANE, 2026-09-09. Why it earns a slot, and why it is worth filing now: the uk-cpi-2026-09-16 lane explicitly HUNTED this date on 2026-09-09 and did not propose it, recording that 'no Ofgem primary names the date, and a guessed date is worse than a gap'. Ofgem's own 26 August release does name it, and this proposal is that gap closed from the primary rather than from a guess. What it decides: the Ofgem cap steps on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October, and each step is the single largest known mover of the UK CPI housing-and-household-services line — the 1 July 2026 step alone took that division's 12-month rate from 2.7% to 4.1% with gas up 14.7% (ONS July 2026 bulletin). The January 2027 step therefore lands in the January CPI print, and its ANNOUNCEMENT on or before 2026-11-25 is what makes it forecastable. Two dated interactions this calendar already tracks: the announcement falls twenty days AFTER the 2026-11-05 MPC meeting and its November Monetary Policy Report, so the Bank must set its forecast path without it; and it is the last cap set while the electricity VAT zero-rating is in force (uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01, reversing 2027-04-01 per uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01), so the January cap is the one quarter where a headline cap number and the bill a household actually pays diverge by the full 5% VAT.
